t.3.59.1: Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, saw the hermitage empty, the leaf-hut deserted, and the seats scattered and destroyed.
t.3.59.2: Not seeing Vaidehī there, though he had searched everywhere, Rāma cried out aloud and, raising his handsome arms, spoke.
t.3.59.3: Where, O Lakṣmaṇa, is Vaidehī, or to what land has she gone from here? By whom, O Saumitri, has my beloved been carried off, or by whom has she been devoured?
t.3.59.4: O Sītā, if, hiding yourself behind a tree, you wish to laugh at me, enough of your laughter now; come to me, who am deeply grieved.
t.3.59.5: O Sītā, the trusting young fawns with whom you play, these, O gentle one, bereft of you, sit brooding, their eyes clouded with tears.
t.3.59.6: Surely my father, the great king, will see me in the other world, dead from the great grief born of Sītā's abduction.
t.3.59.8: In the other world my father will surely say to me, "Shame on you!", calling me one who acts from desire, ignoble, and a speaker of falsehood.
t.3.59.7: How is it that you, whom I had charged with this task, after giving your promise, have come here into my presence without seeing that time through?
t.3.59.10: Where are you going, O lady of beautiful hips, abandoning me, O slender-waisted one? And separated from you, I shall give up my own life.
t.3.59.9: Abandoning me here, helpless, scorched by grief, wretched and pitiable, my heart's desire shattered, just as fame abandons a dishonest man…
t.3.59.11: Lamenting thus, Rāma, longing for the sight of Sītā, did not see Janaka's daughter, and Rāghava was sorely afflicted with grief.
t.3.59.12: To Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, who could not find Sītā and was sinking like an elephant that has entered a vast mire, Lakṣmaṇa spoke earnestly, wishing for his welfare.
t.3.59.14: Maithilī loves to roam the woods and is enraptured by the forest; she may have entered the forest, or gone to a lotus pond in full bloom.
t.3.59.13: Do not give way to despair, O mighty-armed one; make the effort together with me. For this forest, O hero, is adorned with many caves.
t.3.59.15: Or she may have gone to a river frequented by fish and vañjula birds; or, wishing to frighten us and to test you and me, O bull among men, Vaidehī may be hiding somewhere in the forest.
t.3.59.16: Glorious as you are, let us two strive swiftly in the search for her; if you think it fit, O Kākutstha, we shall search the whole forest for where Janaka's daughter may be. Do not set your mind on grief.
t.3.59.18: The two sons of Daśaratha, searching thoroughly for Sītā, explored the slopes, the caves and the peaks of that mountain.
t.3.59.17: Thus addressed by Lakṣmaṇa out of affection, Rāma, composing himself, began to search together with Saumitri. The two of them searched the forests and the mountains, the rivers and the lakes.
t.3.59.19: Though the two searched thoroughly, they did not find her at all. Having searched the mountain on every side, Rāma spoke to Lakṣmaṇa.
t.3.59.20: "O Saumitri, I do not see Vaidehī here on this beautiful mountain." Then Lakṣmaṇa, burning with grief, spoke these words.
t.3.59.21: Wandering through the Daṇḍaka forest, O greatly wise one, you will find your brother of blazing splendour and Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka.
t.3.59.22: Just as the mighty-armed Viṣṇu, having bound Bali, ruled this earth, so shall you. Thus addressed by the heroic Lakṣmaṇa, that Rāghava…
t.3.59.23: His mind stricken with sorrow, he spoke in a piteous voice: "The whole forest has been thoroughly searched, and the lotus ponds with their blossoming lotuses.
t.3.59.25: Lamenting thus, Rāma, worn down by the abduction of Sītā, wretched and overwhelmed with grief, became distraught for a moment.
t.3.59.24: And this mountain too, O greatly wise one, abounds in caves and waterfalls, yet I do not see Vaidehī, who is dearer to me than life itself.
t.3.59.26: He, all his limbs trembling, his reason gone and his senses lost, afflicted and wretched, sank into despair, heaving a long and burning sigh.
t.3.59.27: Rāma, the lotus-eyed, sighing again and again, cried out repeatedly, "Alas, my beloved!", his voice choked with tears.
t.3.59.28: Then Lakṣmaṇa, his dear kinsman, who knew dharma, humble and with hands humbly joined in reverence, consoled him in many ways.
t.3.59.29: But disregarding those words that had fallen from Lakṣmaṇa's lips, and not seeing his beloved Sītā, he cried out again and again.
